vocabulary.definition: The native utility token of the Pocket Network blockchain used for staking by applications, gateways, and suppliers
A node operator that stakes POKT tokens to provide RPC service to the network. Formerly called a 'servicer' in Morse.
An entity that stakes POKT and routes relay requests from applications to suppliers on behalf of app developers
A blockchain application or developer that stakes POKT to access Pocket Network RPC services
A time-bounded, deterministic matching of applications to suppliers for serving relays, based on on-chain data
A single RPC request routed from an application through a gateway to a supplier node on the network
A blockchain network or RPC endpoint type supported by Pocket Network, identified by a service ID (e.g., 'eth', 'polygon')
A short identifier string for a supported blockchain service (e.g., 'eth' for Ethereum, 'avax' for Avalanche)
Pocket API & Toolkit Harness - an open-source framework for deploying permissionless gateways on Pocket Network
The current protocol upgrade of Pocket Network (launched June 2025), enabling permissionless staking for gateways and suppliers
The legacy version of the Pocket Network protocol, being sunset in favor of Shannon
Cryptographic evidence submitted by a supplier after completing a relay session to claim token rewards
A supplier's on-chain assertion of the number of relays served in a session, prior to proof submission
The act of locking POKT tokens on-chain to participate as an application, gateway, or supplier on the network
The Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus engine underlying the Pocket Network Shannon chain (formerly Tendermint)
The remote procedure call protocol used for blockchain node interactions; all EVM-compatible chains use JSON-RPC 2.0
Grove Inc., a company that operates the Grove gateway (grove.city) on top of Pocket Network's PATH framework
HTTP header required when using production Grove gateway endpoints to identify the developer application
